org: New York Immigration Coalition, Inc.
purpose: This initiative will strengthen the City’s immigration legal services by investing in coordination, direct services to low-income immigrants and technical support for immigration legal providers. Legal services to be provided include eligibility screenings, applications before USCIS such as for humanitarian relief and work authorization, motions before EOIR such as reopening cases, and changes in venue or hearing format, Special Immigrant Juvenile Status, detention support such as in-person or remote visits, petitions for habeas, and bond hearings, court accompaniment, rapid response legal assistance, wrap around services, and other pathways to secure legal immigration status, as impacted by need and demand. In addition, funding may be used to cover filing fees such as with USCIS, EOIR, and the BIA, legal research, costs to enhance data systems, outreach efforts, and emergency relief supplies such as public transit cards to attend court or emergency preparedness kits like in the event of a family member being detained. With prior approval from the City Council, a portion of the funding may also be used to subcontract with attorneys handling specialized immigration cases.
